{{Short description|Concept in formal semantics and philosophical logic}}

In [[formal semantics (natural language)|formal semantics]], '''Strawson entailment''' is a variant of the concept of [[entailment]] which is insensitive to [[presupposition]] failures. Formally, a sentence ''P'' Strawson-entails a sentence ''Q'' iff ''Q'' is always true when ''P'' is true and ''Q''s presuppositions are satisfied. For example, "Maria loves every cat" Strawson-entails "Maria loves her cat" because Maria could not love every cat without loving her own, assuming that she has one. This would not be an ordinary entailment, since the first sentence could be true while the second is undefined on account of a presupposition failure; loving every cat would not guarantee that she owns a cat.<ref name = "HomerBCS">{{cite encyclopedia|title=Negative Polarity|encyclopedia=Blackwell Companion to Semantics |year=2020|last=Homer|first=Vincent|pages=1–39 |editor-first1=Gutzmann|editor-last1=Daniel|editor-last2=Matthewson|editor-first2=Lisa|editor-link2=Lisa Matthewson|editor-last3=Meier|editor-first3= Cécile|editor-first4=Rullmann|editor-last4=Hotze|editor-first5=Thomas Ede|editor-last5=Zimmermann|publisher=Wiley Blackwell|doi=10.1002/9781118788516.sem057|isbn=978-1-118-78831-8 |url=https://semanticsarchive.net/Archive/DMwOTgzO/Homer_Negative_Polarity.pdf}}</ref><ref name ="NYU Notes">{{cite web|author-first1=Masha|author-last1=Esipova|author-first2=Nadine|author-last2=Theiler|author-last3=Champollion|author-first3=Lucas|url=https://bpb-us-e1.wpmucdn.com/wp.nyu.edu/dist/0/10199/files/2020/03/14-lecture-NPIs.pdf|title=Introduction to Semantics: NPIs |date= |website=NYU Introduction to Semantics Fall 2018|access-date=2024-09-21}}</ref><ref name = "sharvit17">{{cite journal |last=Sharvit|first=Yael|author-link=Yael Sharvit|title=A note on (Strawson) entailment|journal=[[Semantics and Pragmatics]]|volume=10|doi=10.3765/sp.10.1|year=2017|pages=1–38 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Strawson entailment has played an important role in semantic theory since some [[natural language]] expressions have been argued to be sensitive to Strawson-entailment rather than pure entailment. For instance, the textbook theory of weak [[negative polarity item]]s holds that they are licensed only in Strawson-[[downward entailing]] environments. Other phenomena that have been analyzed using Strawson entailment include temporal adverbials, covert reciprocals, and [[scalar implicature]].<ref name = "HomerBCS"/><ref name = "NYU Notes"/><ref name = "sharvit17"/><ref name = "AllThingsLinguistic">{{cite web |author-first=Gretchen|author-last= McCulloch|author-link=Gretchen McCulloch|url=https://allthingslinguistic.com/post/113907456893/a-detailed-explanation-of-negative-polarity-items |title=A detailed explanation of Negative Polarity Items and Downwards Entailment, using Mean Girls references |website=All Things Linguistic |access-date=2024-09-21}}</ref> Although the concept is widely used within formal semantics, it is not universally adopted and alternative proposals have argued both for returning to pure entailment and for generalizing the notion further to consider not-at-issue content beyond presupposition.<ref name = "sharvit17"/><ref name = "HomerBCS"/><ref>{{cite journal|last=Barker|first=Chris|author-link=Chris Barker (linguist)|year=2018|title=Negative polarity as scope marking|journal=[[Linguistics and Philosophy]]|volume=41|issue=5|pages=483–510|doi=10.1007/s10988-018-9234-2|url=https://semanticsarchive.net/Archive/zRiMTU0N/barker-negative-polarity-as-scope-marking-final.pdf}}</ref>
